subject: Access evidence deep-dive: SSO/SAML + SCIM ownership artifacts
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@harborhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: security@harborhealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSO/SCIM artifact request and owner map

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. As we discussed we need a compact package of artifacts to validate our SIG/SOC 2 intake:
- representative SAML assertion samples for both interactive SSO and machine-to-machine flows
- a recent SCIM delta snapshot showing user provisioning events for the last 30 days
- an owner-of-record mapping for admin/service accounts and role owners

If you can provide the files or a shared Drive link, Procurement can finish the ingestion. Also note our security team wants an explanation of how ephemeral admin elevation is tracked in audit logs.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Security Architect, Harbor Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO/SCIM artifact request and owner map

Tom / Emma — thanks, got it. I put together an initial plan and small bundle. Two quick clarifications before I drop the artifacts:
1) For SAML samples, do you want full assertions including encrypted attributes or just redacted attribute sets? We can provide both, but redacted PII will speed delivery.
2) For the SCIM delta, do you need the raw audit stream (we can provide a gzipped JSONL) or a parsed CSV of adds/updates/deletes?

Plan:
- I'll attach a short owner-of-record workbook (access-owner-mapping.xlsx) that maps logical roles to owners and last validation date.
- Vanessa will export a 30-day SCIM delta snapshot and a summary sheet with counts by role.
- Jonas will pull 4 representative SAML assertions (redacted) and a short note on where the full assertion logs are stored for audit.

We can also include a 1-page note on ephemeral admin elevation tracking (how we log JIT grants, TTL, and revocation). If you prefer a short walkthrough meeting, happy to set 30 minutes Friday.

Delivering initial artifacts to a shared Drive link by EOD today.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: access-owner-mapping.xlsx (stub)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO/SCIM artifact request and owner map

Tom — attaching the SCIM delta snapshot and a small counts CSV. Notes:
- scim-delta-snapshot.json contains 30 days of provisioning events exported from our SCIM proxy; sensitive fields (email, phone) redacted per our redaction policy.
- summary counts: adds=42, updates=117, deletes=3; most updates are role changes for contractor accounts with TTL.
- We included a short README in the Drive folder that explains the event schema and the provisioning pipeline stages.

For ephemeral admin activity: we tag JIT grants with metadata: requestor, approver, TTL, justification id; revocations generate an immediate audit entry and mail alert. Karthik — tagging you on whether the TTL enforcement is visible in the exported logs or only in the runtime telemetry.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success — Security Intake Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: scim-delta-snapshot.json (stub), scim-counts-202703-202704.csv (stub)

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@harborhealth.com>

Cc: security@harborhealth.com, procurement@harborhealth.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO/SCIM artifact request and owner map

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick feedback after our intake review:
- The redacted SAML assertions look good; can you include one sample with the full Subject/Issuer/NameID (we'll treat it under NDA) so we can validate signature and audience conditions?
- SCIM delta snapshot format is acceptable — can you add a small digest file (sha256) for the exported JSONL so we can verify integrity after transfer?
- Owner workbook is useful. Procurement wants a single-line confirmation from Redwood leadership that the owner mapping reflects authoritative owners as of the last validation date.

If you can provide the digest and the single-line confirmation, Procurement will move the SIG submission to the next step. If needed we can redact more aggressively but having one signed confirmation accelerates the intake.

Would appreciate bullet answers inline here so we have an audit trail.

Thanks — Tom
